The current version almost certainly opens with something generic about "finding out your money personality" or a similar phrase any quiz on earth could use. Replace it with copy that names the specific tension Joel's ICP feels: earning well, spending fine, but somehow never actually building anything. Make the button feel like a small, low-stakes action rather than a commitment. One file edit to QuizIntro.astro, changing the hero paragraph and button label only.

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate from 37.5% closer to the 66.67% Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has an open rate of 37.5% against 16 sends. The Money Vigilance automation, with 12 sends, is opening at 66.67%. The Money Avoidance sequence sits at 52.63%. Money Worship is the clear underperformer. Subject line quality is almost always the single variable separating a 37% open from a 66% open at these small send volumes. The content of the worship sequence itself may be fine; the door is the problem.
proposals.proposal: Replace the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship sequence. The current subject line is almost certainly framing money worship as something to diagnose or overcome, which at the inbox level reads like a criticism before the reader has opted into the conversation. Rewrite it to open with the specific lived experience of a money worshipper: the late-night salary calculation, the feeling that a bigger number would finally settle something. Give the reader a reason to open that feels like recognition, not assessment.

proposals.impact: restore automated content publishing to clear the 1-item queue backlog
proposals.observation: Three GitHub workflow runs failed on 2026-08-24: Daily Blog Post (04:05), Weekly Monday Report (06:24), and Funnel-Hack Digest (09:29). The content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published. The Daily Blog Post failure is the most operationally urgent because it is the machine keeping that queue from running dry. Without a fix, Joel's content pipeline stalls within 24 hours. The only commit in the window was a cursor update, so no human intervened to patch the workflow after it failed.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file and find the failing step. The most common causes at this file path are: an expired API key referenced as a secret, a changed model name in an OpenAI or Anthropic call, or a broken dependency fetch. Check the workflow's run log in GitHub Actions, identify the exact failing step, and patch that step only. Do not alter the workflow trigger schedule or any other step. This is a one-line-or-fewer fix in almost every failure mode of this type. Ship it as a single commit so the next scheduled run at 04:05 UTC succeeds.
